```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(RDBEScore)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_bw())
```

## Introduction

`estimateSrsworTotal()` estimates a population total and its variance for
stratified multistage simple random sampling without replacement (SRSWOR).
It can also calculate variance using Preston's rescaled bootstrap. This
vignette compares the two approaches using complete packaged agricultural
datasets and shows separately why the packaged H8 fisheries example does not
satisfy this estimator's assumptions.

The inputs are `RDBESEstObject`s made with `createRDBESEstObject()`. The outputs
are a table of totals, variances, standard errors and confidence intervals,
optional bootstrap totals, and the checked mapping of sampling stages. No
source dataset is changed. The examples use default strict validation.

The implemented scope requires SRSWOR or census sampling at every stage,
finite numeric observed responses at the terminal stage, and recorded sample
and population sizes that agree with the observed units. Unequal probability
sampling, sampling with replacement and explicit RDBES clustering are outside
this scope. Missing responses are omitted with a warning and no nonresponse
adjustment. A non-census group with only one sampled unit cannot supply an
estimated within-group variance. Its own variance contribution is set to
zero with a warning by default. Both conventions can understate uncertainty.
The agricultural examples below have complete responses and no non-census
singletons.

## What is calculated?

For a single SRSWOR sample with values \(y_1,\ldots,y_n\) from a population of
size \(N\), the familiar estimates are

\[
\widehat{T}=N\overline{y},\qquad
\widehat{V}(\widehat{T})=N^2\left(1-\frac{n}{N}\right)\frac{s_y^2}{n}.
\]

For a multistage design, the calculation works upwards from the terminal
responses. Within a parent and stratum, child totals \(t_i\) and their
estimated variances \(v_i\) give

\[
\widehat{T}_{\mathrm{parent}}=\frac{N}{n}\sum_i t_i,\qquad
\widehat{V}_{\mathrm{parent}}=
 N^2\left(1-\frac{n}{N}\right)\frac{s_t^2}{n}
 +\frac{N}{n}\sum_i v_i.
\]

Independent strata are added within each parent. A census has no variance
from selecting its own units, but retains any variance from sampling below
those units.

The bootstrap resamples within each parent and stratum using SRSWOR
subsamples of size \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), with finite population corrections
and Preston's additive multistage weight recurrence. The bootstrap variance
is the sample variance of the replicate totals. `set.seed()` makes a run
reproducible. Increasing `nBoot` reduces Monte Carlo variation in the bootstrap
variance, but cannot repair unsuitable sampling assumptions.

Both methods report the original estimated total. Their confidence intervals
are normal-approximation intervals,
\(\widehat{T}\mathbin{\pm}z_{(1+c)/2}\widehat{\mathrm{SE}}\), where \(c\)
is `confidenceLevel`. The bootstrap interval is therefore a Wald interval,
rather than an interval from the quantiles of the replicate totals. An
adequate normal approximation is needed for either interval.

## One-stage agricultural example

`Pckg_SDAResources_agsrs_H1` contains the complete 300-county SRS example
converted from `SDAResources::agsrs`. The real sampling stage is represented
by VS. The response `SAsampWtMes` contains agricultural acreage (`acres92`),
so the estimated total is in acres. These fields do not describe vessel
weights in this teaching dataset. The lower tables are artificial census
links needed to represent the data in hierarchy 1.

```{r agsrs-input}
H1SrsDataObj <- Pckg_SDAResources_agsrs_H1
H1SrsEstObj <- createRDBESEstObject(H1SrsDataObj, 1, stopTable = "SA")

unique(as.data.frame(H1SrsDataObj$VS)[
  c("VSselectMeth", "VSnumSamp", "VSnumTotal")
])
```

The packaged FO table declares a census of ten units for each FT, while only
one FO link is present. The dataset preparation identifies these as dummy
tables, rather than an additional agricultural sampling stage. We therefore
explicitly identify FO as a one-to-one census link with `censusLinks = "FO"`.
The resulting warning remains visible. This option changes the effective
counts for estimation and preserves the source data and declared counts in
the returned design. It should only be used when this interpretation is
documented, never to bypass an incomplete real census.

```{r agsrs-estimation}
set.seed(278)
srsResult <- estimateSrsworTotal(
  H1SrsEstObj, "SAsampWtMes", nBoot = 499,
  censusLinks = "FO"
)
knitr::kable(srsResult$estimates, digits = 2)

unique(srsResult$design[
  c("table", "n", "N", "originaln", "originalN", "method")
])
```

We can check the analytical result directly against the one-stage formula.
There is one terminal observation per sampled county. This relationship is
checked explicitly before using the flattened estimation object.

```{r agsrs-reference}
srsValues <- as.data.frame(H1SrsEstObj)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(srsValues$VSid),
          nrow(srsValues) == unique(srsValues$su1numSamp),
          length(unique(srsValues$su1numTotal)) == 1)

y <- srsValues$SAsampWtMes
n <- length(y)
N <- unique(srsValues$su1numTotal)
referenceTotal <- N * mean(y)
referenceVariance <- N^2 * (1 - n / N) * stats::var(y) / n

mc <- estimMC(y, rep(n, n), rep(N, n), method = "SRSWOR")
existingSrs <- doEstimationForAllStrata(H1SrsEstObj, "SAsampWtMes")
existingSrs <- existingSrs[existingSrs$recType == "VS", ]

srsComparison <- data.frame(
  method = c("Direct SRSWOR formula", "estimMC",
             "doEstimationForAllStrata", "estimateSrsworTotal"),
  total = c(referenceTotal, mc$est.total,
            existingSrs$est.total, srsResult$estimates$est.total[1]),
  variance = c(referenceVariance, mc$var.total,
               existingSrs$se.total^2, srsResult$estimates$var.total[1])
)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(srsComparison$total,
                          rep(referenceTotal, nrow(srsComparison)))),
          isTRUE(all.equal(srsComparison$variance,
                          rep(referenceVariance, nrow(srsComparison)))))
knitr::kable(srsComparison, digits = 2)
```

The comparison uses only the genuine VS sampling stage from the existing
estimator. The complete dataset is passed to both workflows.

## Stratified agricultural example

`Pckg_SDAResources_agstrat_H1` is the complete stratified 300-county example.
VS identifies the four regional strata, and `SAsampWtMes` again contains
acreage. Its artificial census links have consistent one-to-one counts and
need no explicit override.

```{r agstrat-estimation}
H1StratDataObj <- Pckg_SDAResources_agstrat_H1
H1StratEstObj <- createRDBESEstObject(H1StratDataObj, 1, stopTable = "SA")
set.seed(279)
stratResult <- estimateSrsworTotal(
  H1StratEstObj, "SAsampWtMes", nBoot = 499
)
knitr::kable(stratResult$estimates, digits = 2)
```

A direct stratified calculation adds \(N_h\overline{y}_h\) and
\(N_h^2(1-n_h/N_h)s_h^2/n_h\) across the independent regional strata.

```{r agstrat-reference}
stratValues <- as.data.frame(H1StratEstObj)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(stratValues$VSid))
byStratum <- split(stratValues, stratValues$su1stratumName, drop = TRUE)
stratReference <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(byStratum), function(stratum) {
  d <- byStratum[[stratum]]
  n <- nrow(d)
  N <- unique(d$su1numTotal)
  stopifnot(length(N) == 1, n == unique(d$su1numSamp))
  data.frame(stratum = stratum, n = n, N = N,
             total = N * mean(d$SAsampWtMes),
             variance = N^2 * (1 - n / N) * stats::var(d$SAsampWtMes) / n)
}))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(sum(stratReference$total),
                          stratResult$estimates$est.total[1])),
          isTRUE(all.equal(sum(stratReference$variance),
                          stratResult$estimates$var.total[1])))
knitr::kable(stratReference, digits = 2)
```

The bootstrap totals show variation from resampling the observed sample
under the specified design. The vertical line is the original total.

```{r bootstrap-distribution, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.5}
ggplot(data.frame(total = stratResult$replicates / 1e6), aes(x = total)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = stratResult$estimates$est.total[1] / 1e6,
             linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Bootstrap total (million acres)", y = "Number of replicates")
```

Exact analytical agreement with a reference calculation checks the
implementation for these examples. A bootstrap variance based on a finite
number of replicates will generally differ from the analytical variance.
Neither agreement nor successful rendering establishes confidence-interval
coverage for a particular scientific application.

## Multistage verification and available examples

The agricultural examples have one genuine sampling stage. Their artificial
census links do not demonstrate sampling at several stages. The current
packaged datasets do not provide an unchanged, complete-response multistage
example meeting all the restrictions above. The closest candidate,
`Pckg_survey_apiclus2_H1`, samples districts and then schools by SRSWOR, but
contains **six** missing enrollment responses, although its help page reports
four. It also requires the documented artificial FO census-link treatment.
Other candidates require explicit clustering or have unknown population
sizes. The H8 example below has a replacement stage.

The regression tests therefore include an independent complete synthetic
three-stage design. Every parent samples two of four units at each stage.
The eight terminal responses are `c(1, 3, 4, 8, 2, 6, 10, 20)`. Hand
calculation gives a total of 432 and a variance estimate of 25,344. The tests
enumerate all 128 equally likely bootstrap outcomes and verify their mean
and variance against those values. This checks the recurrence beyond two
stages. Selecting a complete real multistage reference for scientific review
remains open.

## H8 as a separate example

The complete `H8ExampleEE1` object represents an Estonian sprat sampling
example. Its commercial sampling data, vessel details and species lists
passed RDBES upload screening and were downloaded on 2026-10-14. CL and CE
were attached locally and have not passed upload checks. The existing
unbiased-estimation vignette describes this example in more detail.

First inspect its actual stage metadata, without recoding the sampling
methods or removing records.

```{r h8-design}
H8DataObj <- H8ExampleEE1
validateRDBESDataObject(H8DataObj, checkDataTypes = TRUE)
H8EstObj <- createRDBESEstObject(H8DataObj, 8, stopTable = "SA")

h8Design <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("TE", "VS", "LE", "SS", "SA"),
                                function(tableName) {
  d <- as.data.frame(H8DataObj[[tableName]])
  unique(data.frame(table = tableName,
                    method = d[[paste0(tableName, "selectMeth")]],
                    n = d[[paste0(tableName, "numSamp")]],
                    N = d[[paste0(tableName, "numTotal")]]))
}))
knitr::kable(h8Design, row.names = FALSE)
```

TE uses SRSWOR, but VS uses **SRSWR**, which is outside the new estimator's
scope. SA also contains non-census singleton samples. The default zero
variance convention cannot resolve the unsupported VS sampling method.
Changing the VS code to SRSWOR would change the assumed design and is not
justified by the packaged data. This call deliberately demonstrates the
informative error,
which is caught so that the vignette remains runnable.

```{r h8-scope-error}
tryCatch(
  estimateSrsworTotal(H8EstObj, "SAsampWtMes", nBoot = 99),
  error = function(e) cat("Cannot use the SRSWOR estimator:",
                           conditionMessage(e), "\n")
)
```

The existing `doEstimationForAllStrata()` supports more selection methods.
It can be run on the complete H8 input independently of the new estimator.
Here the response is converted from grammes to tonnes in a copy of the
estimation object. Only the display is restricted to TE month strata after
estimation. Any warnings remain visible.

```{r h8-existing-estimator}
H8TonnesEstObj <- data.table::copy(H8EstObj)
H8TonnesEstObj$SAsampWtMes <- H8TonnesEstObj$SAsampWtMes / 1e6
h8Existing <- doEstimationForAllStrata(H8TonnesEstObj, "SAsampWtMes")
h8Months <- h8Existing[h8Existing$recType == "TE",
                       c("stratumName", "est.total", "se.total")]
h8Months <- h8Months[order(match(h8Months$stratumName, month.name)), ]
knitr::kable(h8Months, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Existing estimator results by month, in tonnes.")
```

These are outputs from the existing workflow, not a validation of its
uncertainty estimates for this design. In particular, a non-census singleton
does not identify its own within-group sampling variance. No bootstrap
comparison or confidence interval from `estimateSrsworTotal()` is supplied
for this H8 example.

## Choosing an implementation

The investigation of [IEOstats](https://github.com/joel-ieo/IEOstats)
motivated this restricted implementation. The relevant concepts are
analytical recursion for SRSWOR/census totals and the multistage rescaled
bootstrap. They are implemented directly with base R and the existing
`data.table` dependency, rather than adding IEOstats as a package dependency.
This keeps the supported assumptions and the mapping from RDBES stages
explicit. The bootstrap follows the additive recurrence in Preston (2009),
including the finite population corrections at successive stages.

The source inspection used IEOstats commit
[`f16a367`](https://github.com/joel-ieo/IEOstats/commit/f16a367976c9d5aebd0e613208e7b1ee8c72ae03).
In that snapshot, `svy_total()` converts caller data with `setDT()` and
manages temporary columns by reference. Its default method vector reaches
a scalar `if` condition without being reduced to one method. Analytical
intervals use a Student's *t* quantile with the original row count minus one
as degrees of freedom. Bootstrap intervals use replicate quantiles.
[Inspected `svy_total()` source](https://github.com/joel-ieo/IEOstats/blob/f16a367976c9d5aebd0e613208e7b1ee8c72ae03/R/svy_total.R).
The new workflow preserves input tables, selects bootstrap execution through
`nBoot`, and explicitly labels its normal-approximation intervals.

The upstream cumulative weight-ratio update also differs from Preston's
equations after two stages. Writing \(A_r\) for the cumulative adjustment
through stage \(r\), it accumulates \(1/(A_1A_2)\) after stage two instead of
\(1/A_2\). The three-stage combined weight consequently has an extra division
by \(A_1\).
[Inspected bootstrap source](https://github.com/joel-ieo/IEOstats/blob/f16a367976c9d5aebd0e613208e7b1ee8c72ae03/R/rs_boot_iteration.R).
Computing the combined adjustment directly avoids these intermediate
divisions. The exhaustive three-stage check above verifies the resulting
bootstrap moments against independently calculated values.

Missing response contributions are omitted from point and bootstrap totals
with a warning, while the original design counts and sampling units are
retained. No nonresponse weighting adjustment is made. This convention does
not establish that the missing values are true zeroes, and the result may
not estimate the full population total. Analytical variance, standard error
and interval limits are unavailable (`NA`) if any responses are missing.
Bootstrap variance describes the retained response contributions and does
not account for nonresponse uncertainty. The two uncertainty methods need
not agree for incomplete responses. An entirely missing response vector is
rejected.

For non-census singleton groups, the default `singleton = "zero"` produces a
warning and sets their own variance contributions to zero. Variance from
sampled descendants is retained. This convention can understate uncertainty.
Use `singleton = "fail"` to stop instead and require the design problem to
be resolved before estimation. Neither convention makes SRSWR or unequal
probability designs supported. These defaults were selected for this
workflow, rather than inferred to be scientifically appropriate for every
dataset.

This vignette and the new estimator were developed with AI assistance.
Human review of the new method, implementation and examples is pending.

## References

Preston, J. (2009). Rescaled bootstrap for stratified multistage sampling.
*Survey Methodology*, **35**(2), 227-234.
[Statistics Canada paper](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/12-001-x/2009002/article/11044-eng.pdf).

The [survey package implementation of the multistage rescaled bootstrap](https://github.com/cran/survey/blob/master/R/mrb.R)
provides an additional reference implementation for this method.
